_comment: What is expected of the next actor, one entry per factory:* state.
This is FACTORY.md §3's 'Advanced by' column as data, so that the two
engines say the same thing and say it every time. Both read this file
out of the factory checkout they already make: the Actions pipeline via
factory_orchestrator.next_step. Change the wording here and both engines
change together — never copy a line into an engine.
Placeholders: {issue} the issue number, {approvers} the gate's approver
list rendered as '@a, @b' (or 'any owner, member or collaborator' when
the list is empty). 'who' is the actor; 'how' is the exact move, and it
must name a real control — a comment to type, a PR to merge, a button,
or a role to start. 'An agent will pick it up' is only true where the
pipeline actually routes the state on its own.

factory:backlog.who: gate G0, on this issue's release tracker
factory:backlog.how: This issue is parked until its milestone is approved. On the tracker issue for its milestone, a release_scope approver comments exactly `Approved`; every backlog issue in that milestone then moves into intake together.

factory:release-planning.how: Comment exactly `Plan release` on this tracker. The Scrum Master reads the milestone, posts the release plan here and moves the tracker to `factory:release-ready`, which is gate G0.

factory:release-ready.how: Read the release plan above, then comment exactly `Approved` here. That releases every issue in the milestone into intake. There is no document PR at G0.

factory:release-approved.how: The milestone's issues are being moved into intake and their Intake Analysts started. Nothing to do.

factory:intake.how: The Intake Analyst is analysing the requirement and will open the spec PR. Nothing to do until it does.

factory:spec-ready.how: Review the spec PR this issue links, then either merge it, or comment exactly `Approved` here — the factory then merges it for you and starts the Planner. Strict match: "Approved, but…" is just a comment.

factory:spec-approved.how: The Planner is breaking the spec into task sub-issues, and chains the Architect in the same run. Nothing to do.

factory:planned.how: The Architect writes design.md and opens its PR — normally inside the Planner's own run. If this issue sits here with no run live, start it: the Factory Console's **Start the Architect** button on this issue, or Actions → "Factory pipeline" → Run workflow (role: `architect`, issue `{issue}`).

factory:design-ready.how: Review the design PR(s) this issue links, then either merge them, or comment exactly `Approved` here — the factory then merges and releases the unblocked tasks for implementation.

factory:design-approved.how: The Dispatcher is marking every unblocked task `factory:ready`. Nothing to do until a task asks for its start approval.

factory:ready.how: Comment exactly `Approved` on this task to start its Implementer, or press **Approve** on it in the Factory Console. Only one start per task: while a run is live the approval is declined, because a second one would put a second Implementer on the same branch.

factory:in-review.how: `factory:in-review` starts nothing on its own. Start the review — the Factory Console's **Start the Reviewer** button on this task, or Actions → "Factory pipeline" → Run workflow (role: `reviewer`, issue `{issue}`). The Reviewer reads the draft PR this task links and moves it to `factory:in-test`, or back to `factory:ready` with changes requested. Reviewed it yourself instead? Comment exactly `Review Done` here to skip the Reviewer and move straight to `factory:in-test` — there is no changes-requested equivalent for that path; if you found problems, review the draft PR directly on GitHub. Do not merge the draft PR yourself either way: review and QA are what make it mergeable, and the Release Manager merges it.

factory:in-test.how: `factory:in-test` starts nothing on its own. Start QA — the Factory Console's **Start QA** button on this task, or Actions → "Factory pipeline" → Run workflow (role: `qa`, issue `{issue}`). QA verifies the WHEN/THEN scenarios, posts the test report here and moves the task to `factory:ready-to-ship`.

factory:ready-to-ship.who: a human, then the Release Manager
factory:ready-to-ship.how: `factory:ready-to-ship` starts nothing on its own. Start the Release Manager — the Factory Console's **Start the Release Manager** button on this task, or Actions → "Factory pipeline" → Run workflow (role: `release`, issue `{issue}`). It merges this task onto its epic branch (or onto the integration branch when the epic has none) and verifies it there.

factory:on-epic.who: the epic, then the Release Manager
factory:on-epic.how: This task is merged onto its epic branch and green there. It waits for the rest of the epic: once every task is `factory:on-epic`, the Release Manager carries the whole epic to the integration branch in one PR. Start that on the **epic** issue, not here.

factory:in-staging.how: The Release Manager's integration report above lists the promotion PR(s) and the order to merge them. Merge them through the GitHub UI, in that order. G3 is deliberately not comment-approvable — `Approved` does nothing here.

factory:deployed.how: In production and soaking. Ops verifies health, archives the change folder and closes this issue — the Factory Console's **Start Ops** button, or Actions → "Factory pipeline" → Run workflow (role: `ops`, issue `{issue}`). File `factory:incident` instead if the deploy regressed.

factory:fast-track.how: The fast lane has no gate and no reviewer: read the PR this issue links and merge it, or say what needs changing here. Nothing else runs on this issue.

factory:blocked.how: An agent stopped and asked a question — it is the newest agent comment on this thread. Reply here with the answer: the factory clears `factory:blocked` and re-runs the stage that halted, re-reading the whole thread.

factory:incident.who: a human, with the Release Manager
factory:incident.how: A post-deploy regression is open. Decide rollback or fix-forward and say which here; the Release Manager carries it out.

factory:profile.how: The Profiler is drafting `.factory/profile.json` and removes this label when it finishes. Re-apply the label to ask for a redraft.

none.who: nobody — this issue is off the rail
none.how: It carries no `factory:*` state label, so nothing routes it. Apply the state it belongs in (`factory:intake` to start it from the top), or leave it: an issue without a state is not the factory's.
